name: LiquidityMapperFast scripts
language: JavaScript-shaped indicator scripts, run once per candle
rules: A script is JavaScript-shaped code run once for each candle of the chart, oldest first, drawing plots from what it reads.

Statements: var, let, const, if / else, for (;;), while, do ... while, break, continue, function name(...) { ... }, return; expressions as in JavaScript, arrow functions and ternaries included. As in JavaScript, a line break ends a statement only where the next line cannot carry it on: x = 1 followed by a line + 2 is x = 3, and a line that starts with ( or [ carries on the line before it. Two statements on one line need a semicolon; end a statement with one when the next line starts with an operator or a bracket.

A name assigned without var, let or const anywhere in the script (x = ...) keeps its value from candle to candle and starts at 0; x[1] is its value one candle back (x[n], n candles back; the first candle reads itself). Such names are one name whatever their case. A var, let or const starts again each candle.

Plot calls, option(...), source(...) and alert(...) take named arguments: line(x, title="CVD", color=red, lineWidth=2); a bare word as a named value is a text (title=CVD). Every other function takes its arguments by position only, and ignores a named one: write sma(x, 20), not sma(x, length=20).

A plot's named arguments are its style, read once, at its first call: what changes from candle to candle goes in its values, by position or in a point object (a mark's text, tip and colour: mark(v, text, tip, colour) or mark({value: v, text: t, color: c}); a line's colour: line({value: x, color: c})).

Plots are line, area, histogram, baseline, candlestick, plotbar, cloudarea, brokenarea, mark (each also as plotline, plothistogram, ...). Each takes title=, priceScaleId=, scaleMargins={top: 0.1, bottom: 0.1} and visible=, and the style its kind reads (see Plots: a candlestick has upColor and downColor, not color); a kind ignores the style it does not read. lineWidth is 1 to 6; lineStyle is 0 solid, 1 dotted, 2 dashed, 3 long dashes, 4 sparse dots. A point can be an object: line({time: time, value: x, color: c}) colours that candle's point.

A script draws in a row of its own under the map, or on the map, where plots on the default price scale (priceScaleId right) stand at their prices and the others on scales of their own; the Draw setting in its panel chooses. $price.color colours the map's candles.

A candle whose flow is known neither from the recording nor from Binance's own candles, or whose liquidations were not recorded (no candle reports them), reads NaN: the functions skip it (they do not take it as 0) and a plot draws nothing there. Use nz(x) where 0 is meant.
Each call of a function with a history (sma, ema, cum, ...) keeps its own: call them at fixed places, not in a loop over windows (a loop would share one).
Lengths may be any expression (sma(x, options.length)); a window shorter than its length uses the values there are.

inputs.name: time
inputs.is: The candle's start, in seconds since 1970 (UTC).

inputs.name: vbuy
inputs.is: Dollars bought at market (taker buys) in the candle, over the markets the script reads (see source). Where the page did not record the flow (before it was opened, or in a gap), the candles of the Binance markets among them say it, spot and perpetual added up, as far back as the script reads (Binance's candles report who bought; no other exchange's do): those markets only, not all of them, so the numbers are smaller there; bar.recorded tells which. NaN where neither is known (a set with no Binance market, or a Binance candle not read).

inputs.name: vsell
inputs.is: Dollars sold at market (taker sells) in the candle, likewise.

inputs.name: lbuy
inputs.is: Dollars of short positions liquidated in the candle (bought back by force), over the markets the script reads.

inputs.name: lsell
inputs.is: Dollars of long positions liquidated in the candle (sold by force).

inputs.name: oichg
inputs.is: Dollars of open interest opened (+) or closed (-) in the candle, over the perpetuals the OI pane adds up (its Venues setting), at the candle's close; NaN where open interest was not read. source(...) does not change it. Also bar.oichg.

inputs.name: cbuy
inputs.is: Trade counts are not recorded here: cbuy and csell always read NaN.

inputs.name: $price
inputs.is: The chart's candle: $price.open, .high, .low, .close, .volume (the chart market's own volume, in coins), .time (seconds). Setting $price.color = "<colour>" colours the map's candle.

inputs.name: bar
inputs.is: The same candle and flow as one object: bar.open, .high, .low, .close, .volume, .vbuy, .vsell, .lbuy, .lsell, .oichg, .timestamp (seconds), and .recorded: 1 where vbuy and vsell were recorded on this page, 0 where they come from the Binance markets' own candles, NaN where neither is known.

inputs.name: renderer
inputs.is: renderer.length is the number of candles so far, this one included; renderer.timestamp the candle's start (seconds), renderer.timeframe its length (seconds); renderer.forming is true on the candle still under way (the newest, until it closes) and false on every closed one; renderer.last is true on the newest candle the script reads, under way or not (a replay, a quiet market), and false on all the others: where a label of the newest value goes.

inputs.name: theme
inputs.is: The page's colours, read-only: theme.dark (whether the chart's background is dark), theme.background, theme.text, theme.up and theme.down (its candles' colours), as colour texts. A script coloured from them follows the theme the person picks, and runs again when it changes.

inputs.name: options
inputs.is: options.name is the value of the option called name (declared with option(...) or set in the panel).

inputs.name: fns
inputs.is: fns[k] is the k-th call of a function that keeps a history (sma, ema, cum, ...), counted in the order they are written; fns[k].state = {} starts it again.

globals.name: option(...)
globals.is: Declares a setting shown in the panel: name = option(default=14, type=number|color|checkbox|text|list|range, label="...", min=, max=, step=, options=[...]).

globals.name: source(x, ...)
globals.is: Reads x over a set of markets: source(vbuy, type=spot|perp, exchange=BINANCE, quote=USDT). Several values in one filter: exchange=BINANCE+BYBIT. Without source, x reads over the flow column's ALL VENUES markets.

globals.name: askdepth(usd) / biddepth(usd)
globals.is: The price at which usd dollars of the order book are passed going out from the candle's close: askdepth up through the asks, biddepth down through the bids, over every book the heat map adds up (source(askdepth(x), exchange=BINANCE) reads some of them). Each candle's book is the one the page recorded at its close: its last minute (a minute is the mean of the samples taken in it), or the latest minute recorded inside the candle where its last was not (never another candle's); the candle under way reads its minute under way. Each recorded bin's dollars are spread evenly over its prices. The close for 0; NaN for a size that is not a number or below 0, where no book of the set was recorded for the candle (before the recording, which reaches a day back in a browser and a week on a server, or more than 1,000 candles back), and where the books hold less than usd on that side. askdepth(x) - close is how far a market buy of x dollars would have moved the price had the book stood still. A server from before reads each candle's book averaged over the candle instead (depthatclose() is false there): a price a candle with a move in it went through held bids part of the time and asks the rest, so the side the price came from reads thin; depthabove and depthbelow do not have that. A call walks the book's bins out to the size: a few steps for most sizes, more for one far into the book.

globals.name: depthabove(usd) / depthbelow(usd)
globals.is: As askdepth and biddepth, over every dollar recorded at each price, bids and asks alike: the price at which usd dollars of the book are passed going up (down) from the close. At a candle's close nearly the same as askdepth (biddepth): they differ in the bin that holds the close, and where the price moved within the last minute, whose prices held some of the other side's orders too. Where the books are averages over the candle (a server from before), the band that reads the book's usual depth instead of a side the averaging thinned.

globals.name: depthatclose()
globals.is: Whether the books read at this candle are their books at its close (true), as the page and an up-to-date server record them, or averages over the candle (false: a server from before); NaN where no book of the set has depth for the candle. It says how the book was sampled, not how fresh it is: where a candle's last minute was not recorded, its latest recorded minute stands in. The Depth bands example reads askdepth and biddepth where it is true, depthabove and depthbelow where not.

globals.name: depthbooks()
globals.is: How many order books of the set read (see askdepth) have their depth recorded for the candle: 0 where none was.

globals.name: alert(text, sound=, when=)
globals.is: An alert: the page lists text and makes a sound, through its Sounds switch (off: nothing happens) and the cap on how many alerts come at once. Only the candle under way and the last closed one alert; each call alerts once a candle, never for what was already there when the script started, and one call at most every 20 s. sound is chime (the default), rise, fall, tick or none (listed, silent). when=bar (the default) alerts as soon as the call runs in the candle; when=close once the candle has closed with the call made. A replay never alerts.

globals.name: nz(x, y)
globals.is: x, or y (default 0) when x is NaN, undefined or null.

globals.name: na(x)
globals.is: Whether x is NaN, undefined or null.

globals.name: rgb(r, g, b) / rgba(r, g, b, a)
globals.is: A colour text. Colours are also CSS texts ("#ff9900", "rgba(0,170,140,0.5)") or names (red, teal, transparent, ...).

globals.name: Math
globals.is: abs, max, min, sqrt, pow, log, log10, log2, log1p, exp, expm1, floor, ceil, round, trunc, sign, cbrt, hypot, sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, sinh, cosh, tanh, random; PI, E, LN2, LN10, LOG2E, LOG10E, SQRT2, SQRT1_2.

globals.name: Number, String, Boolean, Array, Object
globals.is: In part as in JavaScript: Number(x), Number.isFinite, Number.isNaN, Number.isInteger, Number.parseFloat, Number.parseInt and its constants (EPSILON, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, ...); String(x), Boolean(x); new Array(n), Array.isArray, Array.from; Object.keys, Object.values. Texts have slice, substring, toUpperCase, indexOf, includes, split, replace (plain text), padStart, ...; arrays have push, pop, slice, splice, concat, indexOf, join, map, filter, reduce, find, some, every, sort, ...; numbers have toFixed and toPrecision.

globals.name: Date
globals.is: Date.now() and Date.UTC(year, month, day, hours, minutes, seconds) give milliseconds since 1970 (month 0 is January). new Date(ms) takes one number of milliseconds (or a date), not a text and not a year and a month: write new Date(Date.UTC(2026, 0, 1)), or new Date(time * 1000) for the candle. A date has getTime, toISOString, getUTCFullYear, getUTCMonth, getUTCDate, getUTCDay, getUTCHours, getUTCMinutes, getUTCSeconds, and the same without UTC in the browser's time zone.

globals.name: isFinite, isNaN, parseFloat, parseInt, Infinity, NaN, undefined
globals.is: As in JavaScript, except that parseInt reads base 10 unless given a base: parseInt("ff", 16) is 255, and parseInt("0x10") is 0, not 16.

functions.name: cum
functions.is: The running sum of x since the first candle.

functions.name: sum
functions.is: The sum of the last length values of x, this candle included (fewer while fewer exist).

functions.name: sma
functions.is: The average of the last length values of x (of those there are, while fewer exist).

functions.name: cma
functions.is: The average of x and the function's own last length - 1 answers (an average of itself).

functions.name: ema
functions.is: The exponential average: each value weighs 2 / (length + 1); the first value starts it.

functions.name: rma
functions.is: The running (Wilder) average: each value weighs 1 / length.

functions.name: highest
functions.is: The highest of the last length values of x, this candle included.

functions.name: lowest
functions.is: The lowest of the last length values of x, this candle included.

functions.name: linreg
functions.is: The least-squares line over the last length values of x, at this candle.

functions.name: last
functions.is: The oldest of the last length values: x as it was length - 1 candles ago once there are that many (last(x, 2) is the candle before).

functions.name: stoch
functions.is: Where close stands between the lowest low and the highest high of the last length candles, 0 to 100.

functions.name: pivot_high
functions.is: A swing high: the value right candles ago when it is higher than the left before it and the right after it, else NaN.

functions.name: pivot_low
functions.is: A swing low, likewise.

functions.name: avg
functions.is: The average of the values given, the elements of an array given counted one by one. Each is made a number as Number(x) would (true is 1, null 0, "9" 9); those that come out NaN or infinite (undefined, a text that is not a number) are left out.

functions.name: avg_ohlc
functions.is: The chart's candle as {open, high, low, close}, for candlestick(...).

functions.name: avg_ohlc_with_gaps
functions.is: The same as avg_ohlc.

functions.name: avg_close
functions.is: The chart's close.

functions.name: heikinashi
functions.is: Heikin-Ashi candles of the chart's: the close is the average of the four prices, the open the middle of the previous one.

functions.name: avg_heikinashi
functions.is: The same as heikinashi.

functions.name: ohlc
functions.is: A candle of a value: it opens where the previous candle of x closed and closes at x.

functions.name: cum_ohlc
functions.is: A candle of a running sum: it opens where the sum stood and closes with x added (a CVD candle).

functions.name: interpolate
functions.is: The colour at ratio (0 to 1) along the colours given.

plots.is: A line through one value a candle; with lineType=1 each value is a level across its own candle, joined straight to the next (a value on one candle alone draws its level).
A line with the area under it filled.
A bar a candle, from base (default 0) to the value.
A line coloured above and below baseValue, with the areas filled.
Candles from {open, high, low, close} (avg_ohlc, ohlc, cum_ohlc, heikinashi).
Bars (a tick left for the open, right for the close) from {open, high, low, close}.
The area between two values, cloudarea(lower, higher), filled and edged.
A band from lowerValue to higherValue a candle, without joining candles (a row of colour per candle: heat maps).

style: below stands a few pixels clear of the value
offset pixels further off the value
to stack marks of two plots at one candle
plots.is: A mark at a value, on the candles where the call gives one: mark(value, text, tip, colour), or mark({value: v, text: t, tip: s, color: c}). text (up to 24 characters) is shown on the chart; tip (up to 600, a new line with \n) is what the pointer on the mark reads, with the script's name. A value that is not a number draws no mark there. Where marks would cover one another, a label is drawn as a dot and a text alone is left out, so they read when zoomed in.

notSupported: try, catch, throw, switch, class, this, import, export, async, await, yield, delete, with
for ... of and for ... in (use for (var i = 0; i < a.length; i++))
the spread syntax ... and regular expressions (replace takes plain text)
new, except new Date(...) and new Array(n)
single markets by name (EXCHANGE:pair): read markets with source(x, exchange=..., type=..., quote=...)
trade counts: cbuy and csell read NaN
the series, utils and vars objects of chart libraries, and price-scale or series calls
Pine Script: no //@version, no ta.*, no plot(), no close / high / low as bare names (use $price.close), no := (use =)

errors.message: The script ends before this is complete.
Expected X here.
Two statements on one line: put a line break or a semicolon between them.
errors.wrong:
var a = 1 var b = 2
line(a + b)
errors.right:
var a = 1; var b = 2
line(a + b)

errors.message: A name was expected here.
A text is not closed with its quote.
A comment is not closed.
This character cannot be read: X
This number cannot be read.
Unexpected X here.
Only a name, a member or an element can be set.
X is not part of the script language.
Nested too deeply.
errors.note: Reading stops it at brackets or blocks nested about a hundred deep, or at one expression chaining more than 400 operators, calls or members; a run stops it at calls nested deeper than 200 (a function that calls itself without end).
errors.right:
function f(n) { return n >= 10 ? n : f(n + 1) }
line(f(0))

errors.message: Too many different sets of markets: at most 24.
errors.note: A set is one combination of filters (exchange, type, quote). A script has at most 24 sets, the unfiltered one (what x reads without source) always counted among them: 23 source(...) filters that differ.
errors.right:
// at most 23 filters: drop one, or read a wider set (quote= left out reads every quote currency)
line(source(vbuy, exchange=BINANCE))

errors.message: Too many plots: at most 64.
errors.note: Met as the run starts, before the first candle, so nothing is drawn; Check does not count plots. Each plot call written in the text is one plot (a call in a loop is still one).

errors.message: X is not defined.
X is not a function.
Cannot read X of nothing (undefined or null).
X cannot be set.
X is a constant and cannot be set.
X is declared twice.
errors.right:
const a = 1
const b = 2
line(a + b)

errors.message: A break, continue or return outside the loop or function it belongs to.
Stopped: the script took too many steps (a loop that never ends?).
Stopped: an array or a text grew too large.
Stopped: the script took too long.
errors.note: The run took longer than its time: 10 s for a run from the first candle (the chart opened, the script changed), 2.5 s for a live update of the newest candles; each candle on its own stayed within its steps. Work less a candle, or keep in a kept name what an earlier candle worked out. The example below takes about 30,000 steps a candle: it meets the limit on a chart of 2,000 candles.
